notes.title: A New Experimental Netplay Patch!
notes.content:
We're happy to announce a new update to the existing community branch, and a new experimental netplay branch! This branch works on fixing desyncs for various characters, and has breaking changes that are not cross compatible with other branches. See details below!

[h3]Community Netplay Branch[/h3]
Over the years, one of the most commonly reported issues with the netplay system is desyncs. We've managed to identify and fix some instances of this, particularly in matches containing Beatrice and Lambdadelta. This change will be released on the [b]community-netplay[/b] branch as an experimental fix, to be merged into the [b]community[/b] branch depending on your feedback.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31224398/ad7b39026edac707d411dc6f1c46bc94124564b7.jpg[/img]

Please note that matches in the [b]community-netplay[/b] are not compatible with any other branch. Make sure both players are using the same branch when playing against each other.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31224398/8d32ad19740d88ceca0edcde2f8d60e2fcab4570.png[/img]

[h3]New update![/h3]
We also have some new functionality for the existing [b]community[/b] branch. You should now find a menu called [b]Community Edition Settings[/b] with the options listed below:
[olist]
[*] Ability to disable the screen shatter effect when meta is declared. This should help with performance on older computers, especially during online matches.
[*] Various network settings like setting a maximum to rollback frames and rollback cooldown. Give the presets a try if the existing auto-detected settings don't feel quite right.
[*] Ability to show hitboxes and disable stun in training mode.
[/olist]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/31224398/a30f6b5692978805df52638564491e35c47706ea.jpg[/img]

Last but not least, a special thanks and our deepest gratitude to [b]Aria[/b], [b]Hexer[/b], [b]Zanaylo[/b] and [b]Zari0t[/b], as the desync fix in particular would not have been possible without them!

If you have issues, questions, concerns, or just want to find someone to fight, reach out to us on Discord ([url=https://discord.com/invite/xsgJKjh]https://discord.com/invite/xsgJKjh[/url]) or the Steam Forums. We're looking forward to your feedback!

notes.title: Public Community Beta Patch
notes.content:
On December 31, 2010, Umineko: Golden Fantasia's original Japanese release was at Comiket 79. Today, nearly 15 years later it's returning to the hands of independent artists and fans on Steam via [b]a new Community Beta Patch[/b] with support from MangaGamer! 

We have selected:

[url=https://leite.dev/]Sky Leite [/url]
to be the maintainer of the Community Beta Patch. MangaGamer will provide development checks and support on Steam publishing, while Sky will be the Lead Developer of the content on the Community Beta Patch. 

We have a long road map for the Community Beta Patch we are planning on elaborating on in future updates, but the initial release has the following long-awaited changes and fixes to Golden Fantasia to help bring it up to date with modern fighting game standards: 

[list]
[*]  Fix incorrect game speed on high refresh rate display monitors.
[*]  Add feature to bind controllers from the main menu.
[*]  Fix previous inability to bind triggers (R2/L2 and RT/LT) on XInput controllers.
[*]  Fix training mode BGM restarting when resetting training mode.
[*]  Fix dummy recording being erased when resetting training mode.
[*]  Add quick-actions to the in-game menu in Training Mode:
[*]     *Select screen position when resetting.
[*]     *Swap positions with opponent.
[*]     *Save states / snapshots (Experimental).
[*]     *Enable / disable training stun.
[*]  Add ability to use D-Pad and Analog Sticks simultaneously on capable controllers.
[/list]
This Community Beta Patch is in [u][b]experimental beta[/b][/u] and will not be activated by default during public beta. There is not yet a definite schedule or time set for this Community Beta Patch and the beta state may be indefinite while patches are being released. Current or future changes are not guaranteed and the default patch will remain the official game release.

To activate the [b]Community Beta Patch[/b], you will have to do so by following the instructions below:
[list]
[*] Open your Steam Library
[*] From a game's library page, select Manage > Properties
[*] Goto Betas and on the top right select "Community Edition" (if this does not show up in the Beta Participation drop down box, please try restarting your Steam Client to clear the cache)
[/list]
For requests and reports, please see the appropriate threads on the Steam Forums for Umineko: Golden Fantasia. 

[b]Additional License Notes[/b]
This mod patch introduces several new assets, contained in the `/assets` directory. This is a listing of their names, authors and licenses.

- button_{A, B, C, D, F1}.png by Sky Leite, remixed from "FREE Keyboard and controllers prompts pack" by "Nicolae (Xelu) Berbece" licensed CC0 https://opengameart.org/content/free-keyboard-and-controllers-prompts-pack
- "GUI Sound Effects" by "Davic MdKee (ViRiX)" licensed CC0 https://opengameart.org/content/gui-sound-effects
- stick.png, stick_guide.png by Sky Leite
- Xbox buttons (outlined) by Kenney, licensed CC0 https://kenney.nl

notes.title: Steam Remote Play Now Integrated!
notes.content:
When we set out to ship Golden Fantasia on Steam, we had two goals in mind - localize the title, and make the netplay better than it used to be. The second proved to be a much more difficult, and completely new endeavor for those of us at MangaGamer.

For the English localization team, lead by a small group of former Melty Blood players - endeavored to improve the total experience of playing the game. At the time, outside of GGPO and closed-source alternatives, rollback netplay was the most available, successful, and well-documented. MadScientist had worked on this form of networking extensively, and graciously accepted work with us to implement rollback netplay. It was later maintained by our on-team staff to solve configuration options after release.

However, as we opened up to a larger pool of players we found that rollback netplay was not always the best solution. Though it did allow for lower ping and smoother gameplay - there was a key problem on some chipsets. Rollback netplay had always been primarily designed on 2D retro games. While Golden Fantasia is 2D, it uses plenty of graphically intense special effects, which were very new when the game was initially released in Japan. Depending on the hardware, rolling back these intense graphical effects could sometimes cause an undetectable desync between the players.

Though these instances are few and far between, something we have wanted to have is an alternative solution without undoing the dream of low-latency doujin game netplay.

[b]So today we want to offer that new option[/b], and a new way to play all together, to anyone who may be affected by desyncs - and that is the integration of Steam Remote Play and also Steam Broadcasting - for those who have wanted to stream their games and broadcast in lobbies of sorts.

More Setup Details Here: https://steamcommunity.com/app/550340/discussions/0/3074243590157862304/

notes.title: Debate witches with your fists in VN turned fighting game Umineko: Golden Fantasia
notes.content:
Fighting game fans looking for something a little stranger than usual to fill out their library are in for a treat today. Based on the popular Umineko: When They Cry visual novels (which are also available on Steam), Golden Fantasia transplants the cast from their regular, dreary lives as metatextual murder-mystery characters into a no-holds-barred 2v2 tag-team brawl.

While the very first edition of this game came out all the way back in December 2010, this is the officially localised, polished and finalised version of the Cross release, a major expansion which bumped up the size of the playable cast to a respectable 19.

(more…)

notes.title: Umineko: Golden Fantasia Now on Sale!
notes.content:
Drawing from the highly-acclaimed visual novel, this 2D tag-team fighting game features 19 different characters from the series that can be paired to create a wide variety of different match-ups! Combine meta world abilities and fighting styles between partners to create your best tag-team for crushing the competition! Change-up your tag-outs to control the flow the battle--whether pressing an attack, halting a rushdown, escaping from potential stun or guard break, or to recover chip damage--timing your tag is an important key to victory!

Featuring rollback netplay, online and local multiplay versus modes, achievements, and a single-player story mode this exciting new fighting game is now available from MangaGamer on Steam!

To celebrate the release, we also have an official discord server for Golden Fantasia and plans for multiple tournaments are already underway! So if you love fighting games and are looking to test your skill against others in official match-ups, be sure to join the channel and stay in the loop:

https://discord.gg/xsgJKjh

The first official tournament runs in a week, so get training!

notes.title: Netplay Rollout and Live Testing!
notes.content:
Hello Everyone! 

Today, we, poverty anime fighting game players and umineko fans alike, will start mashing on our new completely overhauled netplay system for Golden Fantasia (Ougon/OMK)! If you would like to learn what rollback is, we [url=http://blog.mangagamer.org/2017/12/07/golden-fantasia-rollback-netplay/]invite you to check our blogpost[/url] and learn about the concepts behind bringing you low-delay netplay for fighting games!

Every rollout is not without it's difficulties. Golden Fantasia is a title with very heavy effects, which can cause CPU issues while rewinding on rollback. While we tested each character in the game, we are expecting some desyncs to occur during the release week of Golden Fantasia. 

The good news is, you, as a player, [b]can directly contribute to improving the netcode of Golden Fantasia[/b] and help us diagnose common issues which lead to desyncs and laggy netplay. And here's how! 

[url=http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31224398/739e821a34a1b212f7742682e9dffccb4e3a3f8b.jpg][img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/31224398/e08e9521a3758371c1a3db010a48a280c94d48b9.jpg[/img][/url]

Grab a friend, and enable debug mode when you create a game. Debug Mode will allow you to record extra logs to help us analyze netplay results. 

Normally you wouldn't want to enable this option, since it does increase logging and thus lag on your CPU. While it's on, play with your opponent. Every game you play will create a file, "debug.log" in your Steam folder, likely under C:\Program Files (x86)\Steam\steamapps\common\Umineko Golden\

Debug.log will disappear and recreate each time you relaunch the game, so anytime you experience a desync, close the game, and pull this file. 

Then, both you AND your opponent can submit their debug.log files for the same gameplay session to #bugreporting on our [url=https://discord.gg/xsgJKjh]community discord[/url]. 

From there, we will be analyzing game logs all week to make the netplay better and iron out all the wrinkles with the netplay over release week!
